question: What's the difference between the "standard" Investor KITAS (E28A) and the "Golden Visa" family (E28B–E28G)?
answer:
E28A is the baseline Investor KITAS — the one most PT PMA directors, commissioners, and active
shareholders use. It's tied to your role in a specific PT PMA (minimum IDR 10 billion company
shareholding, per official immigration criteria), runs for 1 or 2 years at a time, and needs a
sponsor arrangement through the company. The E28B–E28G codes are Indonesia's actual "Golden Visa"
program: much larger capital commitments (from USD 350,000 up to several million, depending on the
route), but in exchange you get 5 or 10-year validity in one shot, no need for the same sponsor
structure, and immigration priority handling (we confirm the exact no-sponsor status per code before
filing — it's already confirmed for E28D, and we verify it again for whichever code fits you). Golden
Visa is the right conversation if you're deploying serious capital and want long-term certainty
rather than renewing every 1-2 years.

question: There are 7 different investor/Golden Visa codes (E28A through E28G) — how do I know which one is mine?
answer:
Think of it by HOW you're investing, not by memorizing letters. E28A: you're a director,
commissioner, or active shareholder of a PT PMA — the standard, non-Golden-Visa track. E28B: you're
personally establishing a new company at Golden Visa scale (USD 2.5M for 5 years / USD 5M for 10
years). E28C: you're not setting up a company at all — you're buying Indonesian government bonds,
listed shares, or mutual funds (USD 350,000 for 5 years / USD 700,000, or USD 1M in property, for 10
years). E28D: you represent a foreign parent company establishing a branch or subsidiary in
Indonesia, as a board member or commissioner — a large, corporate-level commitment. E28E: a
Special Economic Zone investor track. E28F: the same branch/subsidiary structure as E28D, but
specifically for Indonesia's new capital (IKN/Nusantara), at a government-incentivized lower
threshold (USD 5M for 5 years / USD 10M for 10 years). E28G: you're a representative of the foreign
parent company assigned to its Indonesian branch — a related but distinct role from E28D's
board-member route. We'll match you to the right one once we know your capital route and whether a
company is involved.

question: What exactly does E28B (Golden Visa — company establishment) require?
answer:
E28B is for someone personally setting up a new company in Indonesia at Golden Visa scale. You
commit a minimum of USD 2,500,000 for the 5-year visa, or USD 5,000,000 for the 10-year visa, and
that commitment must be fulfilled within 90 days of your entry into Indonesia. You'll need audited
financial statements from an internationally-accredited firm showing your shareholding or the
company's revenue, a valid passport (minimum 6 months), proof of at least USD 2,000 in living
funds (shown via a 3-month bank statement), a recent photo, CV, and travel itinerary. Once approved,
government processing after payment is typically about 5 working days — that's the government's
internal turnaround, not the full document-preparation timeline.

question: What does E28C (portfolio/capital-market Golden Visa) require, and can I qualify without setting up a company at all?
answer:
Yes — E28C is exactly for that. Instead of starting a company, you invest in Indonesian government
bonds, shares of publicly-listed companies, or mutual funds. For the 5-year visa you need a minimum
of USD 350,000 in those instruments; for the 10-year visa, USD 700,000 in the same instruments, OR
USD 1,000,000 in Indonesian property instead. You'll need proof of those holdings, a passport valid
at least 6 months, 3 months of bank statements showing at least USD 2,000 in living funds, a photo,
CV, and travel itinerary. This is generally the fastest-to-qualify Golden Visa route for someone who
doesn't want operational involvement in a business.

question: What is E28D and who actually qualifies for it?
answer:
E28D is for someone acting as a board member or commissioner representing a foreign parent company
that is establishing a branch or subsidiary in Indonesia. This is a corporate-scale Golden Visa
route, not a personal-capital one — the investment commitment tied to it is materially larger than
E28B or E28C, reflecting the foreign company's total commitment rather than your personal net worth: the official immigration page states a minimum foreign-company investment of USD 25,000,000 for the 5-year visa and USD 50,000,000 for the 10-year visa, each to be committed within 90 days of entry.
Government data shows E28D behind the large majority of total Golden Visa investment value recorded
in Indonesia (over Rp 50 trillion out of Rp 52.1 trillion program-wide), which tells you this is a
corporate-heavyweight lane, not an individual-investor shortcut. We've now cross-checked this figure
against the official page on two independent occasions and it holds steady, so book a call and we'll
walk through what an 8-figure commitment of this scale looks like for your structure.

question: What's the E28F route for Indonesia's new capital (IKN/Nusantara), and why is the threshold lower than E28D?
answer:
E28F is the same structural route as E28D — representing a foreign parent company establishing a
branch or subsidiary — but specifically for a company located in IKN, Indonesia's new capital in
East Kalimantan. The government deliberately set a lower bar to attract investment there: USD
5,000,000 for the 5-year visa, USD 10,000,000 for the 10-year visa (both due within 90 days of
entry) — noticeably lower than the equivalent non-IKN corporate route. This is a genuine government
incentive, not a typo: Indonesia publicly cut the original IKN Golden Visa thresholds by roughly 80%
to accelerate the capital's development.

question: What is E28G, and how is it different from E28D?
answer:
E28G is for someone formally representing a foreign parent company that has assigned them to its
Indonesian branch — distinct from E28D's board-member/commissioner role in setting up that branch.
Structurally the codes sit in the same "corporate representation" family and the official page
lists similar large investment figures to E28D. This is a corporate-representative route best
scoped in a direct consultation rather than a WhatsApp quote given the scale involved.

question: Across the whole Golden Visa family, what actually determines whether I get the 5-year or the 10-year version?
answer:
It's purely the capital amount you commit — every code in the family (B, C, D, F, G) has two tiers,
and the 10-year tier simply requires roughly double the 5-year threshold (in E28C's case, the
10-year tier can alternatively be met with a USD 1,000,000 property purchase instead of the higher
cash/securities amount). We found no published mid-term "upgrade" application on the official
pages — you choose your tier upfront based on how much you're committing, and the visa is issued
directly at that duration, as far as the public documentation shows.

question: What documents do I need across the Golden Visa (E28B–G) family, in general?
answer:
The government's baseline document list is consistent across the whole Golden Visa family: a
passport valid at least 6 months, proof of living funds (minimum USD 2,000 or equivalent, shown via
a 3-month bank statement), a recent color photograph (within the last year), a CV/resume, a travel
itinerary, and a written commitment statement about your investment amount. For the
company-establishment routes (E28B/D/F/G) you'll also need audited financial statements from an
internationally-accredited firm. On top of this baseline, each code adds its own proof of the
specific investment instrument (a bonds/shares statement for E28C, capital deposit/company
financials for E28B/D/F/G, a property deed for the property-route options).

question: How long does the whole process take, from application to KITAS in hand?
answer:
The government's own processing window, once your documents are complete and payment is made, is
about 5 working days for the visa approval itself. That's not the full timeline, though — there are
actually two separate 90-day clocks to keep straight. First, the visa itself is valid for 90 days
from the date it's issued — you need to enter Indonesia within that window, or the visa lapses and
you'll need to reapply. Second, once you've actually entered Indonesia, a further 90 days start
running from your entry date, and it's THAT window you need to complete your investment commitment
within — a separate, later clock from the visa-validity one. Realistically, count on several weeks
total once you factor in gathering audited financials, proof of funds, and (for company routes) the
actual capital transfer — we'll give you a specific, document-by-document timeline once we know your
exact route.

question: What government fees (PNBP) apply, separate from any service fee?
answer:
For the E28B/C/D/F/G Golden Visa family, the official government PNBP structure currently published
is: IDR 13,000,000 total for the 5-year tier (residence permit IDR 7,000,000 + visa IDR 500,000 +
verification II IDR 2,000,000 + re-entry permit IDR 3,500,000), and IDR 19,500,000 total for the
10-year tier (residence permit IDR 12,000,000 + visa IDR 500,000 + verification II IDR 2,000,000 +
re-entry permit IDR 5,000,000). These are pure government charges set by regulation — separate from,
and unrelated to, any professional service fee — and they can change when the government updates its
fee schedule, so we always confirm the current amount before filing.

question: Can my spouse and children come with me on a Golden Visa?
answer:
Yes, family inclusion is one of the standard benefits of the Golden Visa program generally — the
government explicitly markets "family facilitation" as part of the offering. In practice, your
spouse and dependent children apply for their own linked Family Visa (a separate E31-series code)
once your Golden Visa is confirmed, rather than being automatically included on your document. We'll
scope the family application alongside yours so timelines line up.

question: Can I actually work or operate a business on a Golden Visa, or is it purely a residence permit?
answer:
The E28A page (the base investor track) explicitly describes activities including "investment
activities, business operations, company establishment, and directorship/board membership roles" —
so managing/directing is squarely allowed. The distinction that matters is between DIRECTING a
company (permitted) and personally performing operational, hands-on work that the company sells as
its service (which typically requires a separate Working Visa/KITAS with an approved RPTKA work
plan, not just the investor permit). This distinction applies to the Golden Visa family the same way
it applies to E28A. If you're a hands-on operator — not just a director — flag that early so we
scope the right combination.

question: What happens if I get the Golden Visa but don't complete the investment within 90 days of entering Indonesia?
answer:
All the Golden Visa codes we checked (E28B, C, D, F, G) explicitly require the investment commitment
to be fulfilled within 90 days of your entry into Indonesia — this is stated directly on the
government's own visa pages. We don't yet have a documented answer for exactly what enforcement
action follows a missed deadline (revocation, downgrade, or a grace period), so we'll flag this
honestly rather than guess: if timing is tight for your capital transfer, tell us before you travel
so we can plan the entry date around your funding readiness, not the other way around.

question: After holding a Golden Visa or Investor KITAS for years, can I get permanent residence (KITAP)?
answer:
Yes — Indonesia's investor path to KITAP (permanent residence) exists and is well-established, and
both key numbers behind it are now confirmed directly from the governing regulation's own text. You
need at least 3 consecutive years of continuous residence on a qualifying limited-stay (KITAS) permit
before you can apply to convert to KITAP, plus a minimum investment level of **Rp 15,000,000,000 (15
miliar rupiah)** in share ownership — a separate, higher threshold than the earlier Rp 10 miliar
figure tied to the initial 2-year Investor KITAS grant stage. Those are two different numbers for two
different stages of the same journey, not competing figures for the same requirement — don't let one
get quoted in place of the other. Both the 3-years figure and the Rp 15 miliar investment figure are
unchanged by the government's 2024 update to the underlying regulation, so this is settled ground, not
something that needs reconfirming case by case.

question: How does the Golden Visa / Investor KITAS family compare to E33 (Second Home Visa) — which one should I actually apply for?
answer:
They solve different problems. The Golden Visa/Investor family (E28A–G) is tied to an ACTIVE economic
role — you're directing a company, holding securities, or committing capital as an investor, and
several routes let you work/manage the business (the director/manage-vs-hands-on-operator line we
walk through in more detail is confirmed for E28A specifically and extended by analogy to the rest
of the family — worth confirming per-code alongside your specific role, see Q14). E33 Second Home is
a pure residence product: you
park either USD 130,000 in a state-bank deposit or USD 1,000,000 in property, and in exchange you get
up to 5 years of residence (renewable, up to 10 years total) with no requirement to run a business,
no sponsor, and broad freedom to live in Indonesia, travel in and out, and bring family. One critical point: the base E33 Second Home is NOT a work visa — it does not by itself authorize you to work or be employed in Indonesia; paid work still requires a separate work permit/KITAS. (That is the mirror image of the E28 investor routes above — E28 is built around an active economic role, E33 is not.) It's not an investment-into-a-company vehicle, and it doesn't come with the corporate/board involvement that
the E28 family assumes. If you want to actively run or invest in an Indonesian company, look at E28.
If you want long-term residence backed by savings or property with minimal ongoing entanglement, E33
fits better.

question: For E28C (the portfolio/no-company route), what exactly counts as "qualifying investment," and can I switch instruments after I'm approved?
answer:
Qualifying instruments are Indonesian government bonds, shares in publicly-listed Indonesian
companies, or Indonesian mutual funds — USD 350,000 minimum for the 5-year visa, USD 700,000 for the
10-year visa (or USD 1,000,000 in property as an alternative for the 10-year tier only). We don't
have documented confirmation from the official pages of whether you can rebalance or switch between
these instruments after approval while keeping the same visa valid — that's a "confirm before you
act" question rather than something we'll answer definitively today, since moving funds out of the
qualifying instrument could put your visa status at risk if the total value dips below threshold at
the wrong moment.

question: What happens if I overstay or violate the terms of my Golden Visa / Investor KITAS?
answer:
The same overstay rules apply as to any KITAS holder: IDR 1,000,000 per day of overstay, and if the
overstay runs to around 60 days (or fines go unpaid), Indonesia can move to deportation plus an entry
ban (penangkalan). Under the current immigration law framework, that re-entry ban can now run
significantly longer than in the past — we never promise a fixed "you'll only be banned for X
months" figure, because the duration is not fixed by law at a single number and can be extended. For
a Golden Visa specifically, on top of the immigration-wide overstay consequences, we'd also flag —
as a reasoned inference rather than a directly-documented enforcement rule — that failing to
maintain your qualifying investment (letting the deposit/holding fall below threshold, or the
company going non-compliant) is likely a separate risk to the visa itself, distinct from overstay;
worth actively monitoring alongside the calendar date, not something we've found spelled out as an
explicit penalty on the official pages.

question: If I'm already in Indonesia on a tourist or business visa, can I convert onshore to a Golden Visa, or do I have to apply from abroad?
answer:
Onshore conversions between visa types in Indonesia route through the official Bridging Visa
mechanism rather than a direct one-step swap. The basis is now confirmed: Permenkumham 11/2024
created this pathway specifically — labeled "Izin Tinggal Kunjungan dalam rangka peralihan Izin
Tinggal Keimigrasian" — as a Visit Stay Permit valid for a **maximum 60 days, non-extendable**, that
bridges you from your current permit to the next one without leaving the country. You apply for it
within **3 days before your existing permit expires**, and if you file (and pay the fee) before that
expiry, you're protected from an overstay penalty even if processing runs past your old permit's
expiry date. What remains unconfirmed is whether there's a distinct, Golden-Visa-specific onshore
conversion pathway on top of this general Bridging Visa route — we haven't found a
Golden-Visa-specific onshore-conversion page confirming that, so treat this as "the general Bridging
Visa mechanism applies, with a Golden-Visa-specific route to be confirmed for your case" rather than a
guaranteed yes.

question: What are the most common mistakes clients make when going for the Golden Visa / Investor KITAS family?
answer:
The recurring ones we see: confusing E28A (the standard, cheaper, shorter-duration investor route)
with the Golden Visa family (E28B-G) and being surprised by the real capital requirement once deep
into the process; not fulfilling the investment commitment within the 90-day window because the real
time needed for a cross-border capital transfer or company setup was underestimated; treating an
investor/director permit as a general work permit and personally doing hands-on operational work
that actually needs a separate Working KITAS; letting SKTT reporting, LKPM quarterly filings, or tax
compliance lapse — which puts extension and any later KITAP conversion at risk even though the core
investment is fine; and assuming a code exists and is "live" just because it's on the official list —
some Golden Visa sub-categories (like E28E for Special Economic Zones) don't yet have published
operational details, so those need direct confirmation rather than an assumption of standard
processing.

question: What happens at the end of my Golden Visa's 5 or 10-year term?
answer:
The official pages describe every Golden Visa code (E28B, C, D, F, G) as "extendable and convertible
to other limited-stay permits" — so you're not automatically forced to leave or reapply from zero.
In practice, this typically means either renewing within the same track (if you still meet the
investment threshold) or converting toward permanent residence (KITAP) if you've built up enough
continuous years and meet the KITAP-specific investment level (see Q16 — we flag that figure as
needing reconfirmation). We don't have a documented, code-specific renewal fee or process distinct
from the original application on the pages we checked, so we treat renewal terms as "confirm closer
